lines.japanese: パルクレープに戻ると、カウンターの前に女の客がぽつんとひとり立っていた。
lines.english: When I returned to Paru Crêpes, a lone female customer stood at the counter.

lines.japanese: 上は紺のブレザー、下はタータンチェックの短いプリーツスカート。この辺りじゃよく見る制服だ。たしか駅の反対側にある、ナントカって難しい字の女子校。
lines.english: Navy blazer on top, short tartan pleated skirt below. A uniform you saw a lot around here. From that girls’ school across the station, I think, with a name written in some difficult characters.

lines.japanese: そいつはまた、えらく背が小っこくて化粧っ気のない童顔だった。いまどきブラウスを第一ボタンまで閉めて、ネクタイもきっちり結んでいる。夜の繁華街を遊びまわるようなタイプには見えなかった。
lines.english: She was remarkably short, with a bare, babyish face. These days, you rarely saw a girl button her blouse all the way to the throat and knot her tie so neatly. She didn't look like the type to play around the entertainment district after dark.

lines.japanese: つーか、むしろ夜の柳木原では浮いている。こんな時間にこんな場所をこんなションベン臭い小娘がふらふらしてたら、少女趣味のキモいおっさんにさらわれてしまいそうだ。
lines.english: Actually, she stuck out in Yanagihara at night. A little squirt like that wandering around a place like this at an hour like this might get snatched up by some creepy old man with a thing for little girls.

lines.japanese: まあ、どーでもいいけど。
lines.english: Well, whatever.

lines.japanese: 俺は接客の邪魔にならないよう、パル姐さんに声をかけず、黙って車体の前面へまわりこんだ。
lines.english: Careful not to interrupt Paru with a customer, I circled silently around to the front of the van.

lines.japanese: 「いやもう全然さ。ほんっと表面だけ。可愛いもんだよ実際」
lines.english: “No, no, it's all on the surface. Honestly, he's a sweetheart.”

lines.japanese: 「えーでもー、すっごいやんちゃな子だって聞いたんですけどー」
lines.english: “Ehhh, but I heard he’s a really wild one...”

lines.japanese: バケツを置いておとなしくフロントガラスを磨いていると、クルマ一台分の距離を隔てた会話が聞きたくもないのに耳へ入ってくる。
lines.english: I set down the bucket and dutifully polished the windshield. Their conversation traveled the length of one van into my ears, whether I wanted it or not.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや、ありゃあ強がってキャンキャン吠えてるだけさね。べつに噛みつきゃしないんだよ」
lines.english: “No, no, no, he’s just putting up a tough front and yapping. He doesn’t actually bite.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そうなんですかー。あー、意外と多いですよねそういう子ー」
lines.english: “Oh, is that right? You meet a surprising number like that, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 小娘は常連客だったんだろうか。パルさんとなにやら親しげに語りあってる。話の内容から察するに、トークの種は大方チワワかプードルあたりの──
lines.english: Maybe the girl was a regular. She and Paru were chatting like old friends. From the sound of it, they were probably talking about a Chihuahua or a poodle—

lines.japanese: 「で、そいつ、『オイオイ』ぐらいの感覚でやたら『ブッ殺すぞ』とか言いやがんだァ」
lines.english: “And he throws around ‘I'll fucking kill you’ with about the same weight most people give ‘hey, hey.’”

lines.japanese: 「──って、俺かよ！」
lines.english: “—Wait, that's me!”

lines.japanese: 思わず上半身だけ傾けて後ろの会話に割りこんだら、あのちびっこい女と目が合った。まるで土佐犬か地獄の番犬にでも遭遇したみたいに驚いてる（失礼な話）。中でクレープを焼いてるパルさんの姿は見えなかった。
lines.english: Without thinking, I leaned my upper body sideways and cut into the conversation behind me, meeting the little woman’s eyes. She looked as shocked as if she’d run into a Tosa fighting dog or a hellhound. Rude. I couldn’t see Paru making crepes inside.

lines.japanese: 小娘は小指一本分ぐらい口を開け、わりかし間抜けなツラで突如現れた男を見る──
lines.english: Mouth open about the width of a pinkie, the girl looked at the suddenly appearing man with a pretty stupid expression—

lines.japanese: ──が、忘れていた礼儀作法を思いだしたように、慌ててへこっと頭を下げた。
lines.english: —then, as though suddenly remembering some forgotten rule of etiquette, she bobbed her head in a hurry.

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: なんかズレてるやつだ。俺はガラス拭きの手を止めないまま、ついっと顎で礼を返した。べつに俺は店員じゃないから、パル姐さんの客に愛想を振りまく義理はない。
lines.english: Bit of an offbeat one. Without stopping my wiping, I gave a quick nod of my chin in return. I wasn’t an employee, so I didn’t owe Paru’s customers any friendliness.

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　ドラいたの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Dora, you were here?”

lines.japanese: 車体側面のカウンターから、女店主がぬっと顔を突きだした。
lines.english: The woman running the place poked her head out through the counter window in the side of the van.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いるだろ。つか、てめーが命令したんだろブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。水で戻した鳥フン、フロントガラスにまんべんなく延ばすぞ。ほどなくミルキーに延ばすぞ」
lines.english: “No shit, I’m here. You’re the one who told me to do this. I’ll fucking kill you, asshole. I’ll spread the rehydrated birdshit nice and evenly over the windshield. Work it in until it goes nice and milky.”

lines.japanese: 俺がいつものようにドスを利かせた声でぼそぼそ喋ると、小娘は手にしていた紙（なんかの地図に見えた）を後ろ手に回しながら一歩下がった。
lines.english: As I muttered in my usual threatening voice, the girl took a step back, putting the paper she held—it looked like some map—behind her back.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、この子お客さんだよ」
lines.english: “Dora, this girl’s a customer.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　そんなん見りゃ分かるけど」
lines.english: “Huh? I can see that.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうじゃなくて、あんたのお客だよ」
lines.english: “No, that's not what I mean. She's *your* customer.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そんで、ねーちゃん。この男、これがあんたの探してる便利屋」
lines.english: “And, miss, this man here is the handyman you’re looking for.”

lines.japanese: 互いに紹介されて、俺と小娘は改めて相手の姿を確認した。つまり目が合った──
lines.english: Introduced to each other, the girl and I took another look at one another. In other words, our eyes met—

lines.japanese: ──しかし合った瞬間、すぐにやつは視線を下へ落とした。相手の目を見て話すのが苦手なやつにありがちな反応だ。
lines.english: —but the instant they did, she dropped hers. A common reaction from people who weren’t good at looking someone in the eye while talking.

lines.japanese: もちろん俺は視線を動かさなかった。先に目を逸らした方が負けという、いま考えれば意味不明の不文律がはびこる少年時代を過ごしてきたせいで、俺の眼球はいまでも鈍重で可愛げがなかった。
lines.english: Naturally, I didn’t move my eyes. I’d spent my boyhood under an unwritten law that the first guy to look away lost—a rule that made no sense now. So my eyeballs were still sluggish and uncharming.

lines.japanese: 俺の客だという小さな制服姿を、俺は見下ろすように観察する。
lines.english: I looked down and studied the tiny uniformed figure who was supposedly my customer.

lines.japanese: まるで子供だ。アリスと同い年と言ったって通じそう……いや、さすがにそれは言い過ぎだけど、比喩としちゃそんな感じ。そんな小っこいのが俺を訪ねて来た？　誰からの紹介だろう。金は持ってるんだろうか。
lines.english: Like a child. You could say she was Alice’s age and get away with it... No, that was going too far, but as a comparison, something like that. This little thing had come looking for me? Who’d referred her? Did she have money?

lines.japanese: 女は俺の視線が落ちつかないみたいで、硬い会釈をしたきり目を上げない。口も開けない──いや、開けてるけど言葉が出てこない。なんだおい、話進まねえよ。
lines.english: My gaze seemed to make her uncomfortable. After a stiff nod, she wouldn’t raise her eyes. Wouldn’t open her mouth—no, it was open, but no words came out. Hey, we weren’t getting anywhere.

lines.japanese: つーか、口を閉じるか声を出すかどっちかにしろ。無言なのに開けっぱなしだと馬鹿な子みたいだ。
lines.english: I mean, either close your mouth or make a sound. Keeping it open without saying anything makes you look like a stupid kid.

lines.japanese: 「俺になんの用」
lines.english: “What do you want with me?”

lines.japanese: 俺は窓拭きクロスを足元のバケツに放って一歩前へ出た。女が一歩下がる。
lines.english: I tossed the cleaning cloth into the bucket at my feet and stepped forward. She stepped back.

lines.japanese: 「あ、や、そんなですねー、ぜんぜん大した用ではー、ええ、ないんですけどー」
lines.english: “Ah, no, well, you seeee, it’s nothing very important at aaall, nooo...”

lines.japanese: 滑舌はいいけど文節のケツがだらしない、間抜けな喋り方をするやつだった。
lines.english: Her articulation was clear, but the tail of every phrase went slack. It made her sound like an idiot.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう。じゃ、いいじゃん。帰れば」
lines.english: “Oh. Then we're done. Go home.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、あーはい……そう、ですね……」
lines.english: “What? Oh, ah... yes. I... suppose so...”

lines.japanese: 「あはは……えと、はい、それじゃ……お邪魔いたしました」
lines.english: “Ha ha... um, yes, then... sorry to have bothered you.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ちょ、待った！　おい、待った待った！」
lines.english: “What? Hey, wait! Hold on, hold on!”

lines.japanese: ふらーっと逃げそうになった小娘の両肩を、パル姐さんがクルマから飛びだしてきて捕まえる。やつの制服が小麦粉でかすかに白く汚れた。
lines.english: Paru jumped out of the van and caught the girl by both shoulders as she started drifting away. A little flour whitened the girl’s uniform.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ！」
lines.english: “Dora!”

lines.japanese: パル姐は振りかえりざま、網タイツの右足を鋭く前へ突きだした。ショートブーツのソールが俺の膝ぎりぎりをかすめて、ミニバンのゴムタイヤに突きたった。
lines.english: Turning, Paru sharply thrust her right leg forward in its fishnet stocking. The sole of her ankle boot skimmed past my knee and planted itself on the minivan’s rubber tire.

lines.japanese: 「てめえコラ、なにこんな小さい子ビビらしてんだバカヤロー！」
lines.english: “You dumb bastard! What are you doing, terrifying a tiny girl like this?”

lines.japanese: ティアードフリルの超ミニを惜しげもなく縦に開き、膝の上に肘を乗せて女はがなる。角度によっちゃパンツ見えそうだ。見たくもないけど。
lines.english: She didn’t care how her ruffled micro-miniskirt spread as she planted an elbow on her raised knee and bellowed. From the right angle, you could probably see her panties. Not that I wanted to.

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。いつ俺がビビらせたんだよ。ほんのちょっぴり無礼な対応しただけだろ」
lines.english: “What did I do? When did I scare her? I was only the tiniest bit rude.”

lines.japanese: 「なァに言ってゃんでい、そんなメンチ切ってドスの利いた声でおまえ、ええッ？　初対面の女の子相手に冗談じゃないよ？」
lines.english: “What the fuck are you saying? Glaring like that and using that threatening voice, huh? You can’t be serious, acting like that with a girl you’ve just met!”

lines.japanese: 「おう、冗談じゃねえよ。初対面ってのは真剣勝負なんだよ。舐める側ンなるか、舐められる側ンなるか、いっちゃん最初の目ぇ合った瞬間に全部決まンだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, I’m serious. A first meeting’s a serious contest. Whether you’re the one looking down on them or getting looked down on, it’s all decided the very first instant your eyes meet.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なるほどー、それは一理あるかもしれませんねー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, I seeee. That might have some truth to it...”

lines.japanese: パルさんの横で、小娘は他人事のようにうんうんと頷いていた。俺はじろりとそっちに視点を移す。ふと、やつの目元のあたりは誰かに似ていると思った。誰だろう。思いだせない。うん、じゃあいいや。
lines.english: Beside Paru, the girl nodded along as if none of this concerned her. I slid a sharp look her way. Something around her eyes reminded me of somebody. Who? Couldn't remember. Fine, then.

lines.japanese: クレープ屋は車輪の上から足を下ろし、でっかい溜息をこぼしながら腕を組んだ。
lines.english: The crepe seller took her foot off the wheel, folded her arms, and let out a huge sigh.

lines.japanese: 「やれやれだ……あんたもさ、ね、おねえちゃん、いちいちビビってんじゃないよ？　先に教えてやったろ、こいつは無駄に態度でかいだけで、べつに怒ってるとか嫌がってるとかじゃないんだよ。ホントだよ」
lines.english: “Honestly... And you, miss, don't jump at every little thing. I told you already: he just throws his weight around for no reason. Doesn't mean he's angry or doesn't like you. Really.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そうなんですかー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, is that right...”

lines.japanese: 「なー、そうだよなあ坊主」
lines.english: “Right? Isn’t that right, kid?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 小娘が子供みたいに落ちつかない目玉をぴっと固定して俺を見上げた。俺が睨みかえしてみても、今度は目を側めなかった。
lines.english: The girl’s restless, childlike eyes snapped into place and looked up at me. Even when I glared back, she didn’t look away this time.

lines.japanese: かと言って、このままふたり見つめあうのもなかなかキモイので、仕方なく俺は横を向いて「ウッセー」とつぶやいた。
lines.english: But standing there staring at each other was pretty creepy too, so I had no choice but to turn aside and mutter, “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 「わはは、『ウッセー』だってよ。な、かわいいだろ、あいつ。あんな目付きしてるくせにすぐ照れやがンだ、ひひひ」
lines.english: “Wahaha, ‘Shut up,’ he says. See, cute, isn’t he? Eyes like that, and he gets embarrassed right away. Hee-hee-hee.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ツンデレというやつですか」
lines.english: “Ohhh, the hard-shell, soft-center thing?”

lines.japanese: 「は、なんだぃそれ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、なんかネットで見たんですけどー、いま日本にそういう言葉があるらしいですよー？　詳しくは分からないんですけどー、どうも表面と内面とにギャップのある人格を指すみたいでー」
lines.english: “Uh, I saw it online somewhereee. Apparently people are using that term nooow? I don’t know the details, but it seems to mean someone who’s different on the inside than they are on the outside...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そんなら間違いない、こいつのことだ」
lines.english: “Ah, then there’s no question. That’s him.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほどー、それじゃいまはツンなんですねー」
lines.english: “I seeee. So this is the hard shell...”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだてめ、なにあったかい目で見てんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell are you looking at me with those warm, understanding eyes for?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……あ、はい、すみません」
lines.english: “Huh... Ah, yes, sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「すいませんじゃねえんだよ。あァコラ、なに目ぇ逸らしてんだよ。てめ、誰も謝れなんて言っ──」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘sorry’ me. Hey, why’re you looking away? Nobody said you had to fucking apolo—”

lines.japanese: 「バカヤロ。だから、その恐い目付きはよしなってんだよ、この小僧は」
lines.english: “Idiot. I told you to quit with the scary eyes, you little brat.”

lines.japanese: 「痛ってーな、こういう目なんだからしょーがねえだろ。ピンクてめえ、男子の面貌にケチつけてんじゃねえよブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Ow, goddammit. These are the eyes I've got. What am I supposed to do? Pinky, don't criticize a man's face. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「出た。出たよ『ブッ殺すぞ』だ。ほーらこれ、ちっとも恐かないだろ？」
lines.english: “There it is. There’s the ‘I’ll fucking kill you.’ See? Not scary at all, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはー……」
lines.english: “Ah, ahaaa...”

lines.japanese: 小娘は俺ではなくクレープ屋の方へ体を向け、顔の下半分だけでぎこちなく笑ってみせた。
lines.english: Turning toward the crepe seller rather than me, the girl gave an awkward smile with only the lower half of her face.

lines.japanese: パルさんはきひひと笑いかえしながら、もう一回俺の後頭部をはたいた。音は派手だけど実はあんまり痛くない。姐さんは痛そうに見える叩き方の名人だった。
lines.english: Paru answered with a wicked little giggle, then smacked the back of my head again. It made a spectacular sound but barely hurt. She was an expert at making a slap look painful.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、この子はあんたのお客さんなんだよ。あんたも商売人ならね、相応の対応ってもんがあるんじゃないかい」
lines.english: “Dora, she’s your customer. If you’re running a business, you oughta treat her like a customer, don’t you think?”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、いまやろうと思ってたんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. I was just about to.”

lines.japanese: 俺は尖らせた唇から放課後の小学生みたいな弁解を放って、叩かれた個所をがしがしと掻きむしった。
lines.english: Pouting like a grade-schooler after class, I offered that excuse and furiously scratched the spot she’d hit.

lines.japanese: 「あーハイ毎度どーも、あなたの街の便利屋さん成田工務店です」
lines.english: “Yes, hello, thank you for your business. Narita Construction, your friendly neighborhood handyman speaking.”

lines.japanese: いきなり営業スマイルを作れるほど器用じゃないので、開きなおって無愛想なまま客に対峙する。
lines.english: I wasn’t skillful enough to make a sales smile out of nowhere, so I faced the customer with my usual surliness and no apologies.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、どーも……」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. Hello...”

lines.japanese: でっかいリボンを提げたやつの頭はいちおう俺に向いていたが、視線はあきらかに正面から四十度ほど外れていた。
lines.english: The head beneath the enormous ribbon was technically pointed at me, but her gaze sat a good forty degrees off center.

lines.japanese: あー、いるいる。ひとの目を見て話せない子供。
lines.english: Ah, yeah. You met kids like this—the kind who couldn’t look anyone in the eye.

lines.japanese: 「で、なに。俺のこと誰から聞いてきたの」
lines.english: “So. Who told you about me?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はいあの左右田さんから伺いまして」
lines.english: “Ah, yes, um, I heard from Mr. Souda.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は定まらない視線を足元に泳がせながら一息で言った。言葉が伸びない。
lines.english: Her uncertain eyes swam around at her feet as she said it in one breath. No drawn-out words.

lines.japanese: 「ソーダさん。ソーダさん？」
lines.english: “Mr. Souda. Mr. Souda?”

lines.japanese: 俺は口の中で繰りかえした。聞いたような聞かないような名前。柳木原のあちこちで働く俺は、いちいち関わってきた人間の顔と名前をすべて覚えているわけじゃなかった。
lines.english: I mouthed the name to myself. It might have sounded familiar. Then again, maybe not. I worked all over Yanagihara; I couldn’t remember every face and name that crossed my path.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいや。で用件は」
lines.english: “Whatever. What do you need?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、あの、私──」
lines.english: “Yes, um, I—”

lines.japanese: やつは顔を上げて言いかけたが、俺が退屈そうに爪のあいだの汚れをほじっているのを見ると、へらへら笑いながら俯いてしまった。
lines.english: She raised her face to speak, but when she saw me picking at the dirt around my nails, looking bored, she lowered it again with a silly smile.

lines.japanese: 「あー、いえ、たはは……あの、すいません、やっぱりいいです」
lines.english: “Ah, no, ha ha... um, sorry. Never mind after all.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh, okay.”

lines.japanese: 俺は爪に息を吹きかけた。小娘は頭の後ろに右手を当てて、何度も細かい会釈を繰りかえした。なんで悪いことしてるわけでもないのに、相手の顔色を窺うみたいにへこへこしてるんだろう。まるで──
lines.english: I blew on my nails. With her right hand behind her head, the girl kept giving little nods. Why bow and scrape like she was trying to gauge the other person’s mood when she hadn’t done anything wrong? Like—

lines.japanese: ──ふと鷲介の媚びへつらった笑い顔を思いだした。あれは俺の嫌いなツラだ。
lines.english: —Shuusuke's ingratiating smile suddenly came to mind. I hated that face.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ。この子、自転車探してるんだってさ」
lines.english: “Dora. She’s looking for her bicycle.”

lines.japanese: おずおずと後ずさり始めた小娘の腕を掴んで、パルさんが言った。
lines.english: Paru said it, catching the girl’s arm as she started timidly backing away.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　チャリンコ？」
lines.english: “Huh? A bike?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい。地方によってはケッタとも言います」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Some places also call them two-wheelers.”

lines.japanese: 俺が横目で小娘を睨むと、やつはテンパってるのかどうでもいい一言を加えた。ひょっとして冗談……なのか？
lines.english: When I glared sideways at her, she added that pointless remark, maybe panicking. Was it... a joke, maybe?

lines.japanese: 「なんかな、きのうこのあたりに置いといて、ちょいとばかし目を離した隙に盗まれちまったんだと」
lines.english: “Seems she left it around here yesterday, took her eyes off it for a little while, and somebody stole it.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「まったくよォ、他人様のもんブン取って自分さえ良ければって馬鹿がのさばってやんだ、バカヤロー冗談じゃねえやチキショーが！」
lines.english: “Honestly! Snatching what belongs to somebody else as long as you get yours—bastards like that running wild! Damn fools! Makes me sick!”

lines.japanese: 人情家のパルさんは気勢をあげて熱く語った。
lines.english: Warmhearted Paru spoke with rising passion.

lines.japanese: 「いや、あのさおばちゃん。熱く語るのは勝手なんだけど、勢いあまって手近にあった俺の頭を平手で叩くのとかやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Listen, lady. Work yourself up all you like, but could you quit getting carried away and slapping the nearest available head, which happens to be mine?”

lines.japanese: くそ、おかげで名前も知らない小娘がビミョーに口角を上げてるじゃねえか。くすくす笑われてる気分だ。
lines.english: Dammit. Now the girl whose name I didn't even know had raised the corners of her mouth a fraction. It felt like she was giggling at me.

lines.japanese: まあ、さっきのへこへこ笑いよりはよっぽどいいけど。あの笑い方は昔からどうも好きじゃない。
lines.english: Well, a lot better than that bowing-and-scraping smile earlier. I’d never liked that kind of smile.

lines.japanese: 「はァ～あ、ひでえ話さね。ねーちゃんあれだろ、鍵だってちゃんと掛けてたんだろ」
lines.english: “Haaah. That’s awful. You had it locked properly too, right, miss?”

lines.japanese: 小娘がついっと無言で頷いた。チャリ泥か。よく聞く話だ。
lines.english: She nodded quickly without a word. Bike theft. Heard about it all the time.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。それはご愁傷様」
lines.english: “Huh. My condolences.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、悼みいります。どんまいです」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. I’m deeply condolenced. Don’t mind me.”

lines.japanese: 俺が適当な言葉をかけると、小娘は真面目くさって頷いた。
lines.english: I offered a token word of sympathy, and the girl nodded with perfect solemnity.

lines.japanese: 「だからドラ、この子の自転車、探してやんなさいよ」
lines.english: “So, Dora, find her bicycle for her.”
“Are you—”

lines.japanese: 吹きだしそうになった。
lines.english: I nearly spluttered.

lines.japanese: 「──馬鹿言ってんじゃねえよ、おい」
lines.english: “—are you kidding me?”

lines.japanese: さらりと無茶を言う。柳木原駅の半径１００メートル内だけでも、いったい何百何千のチャリが転がってるって言うんだ。
lines.english: Such a casually impossible request. How many hundreds or thousands of bikes were lying around within a hundred meters of Yanagihara Station alone?

lines.japanese: いや、それでもまだ、その中にあるって言うなら探す意義はある。しかし。
lines.english: No, even then, if it was among those, there was a point to looking. But—

lines.japanese: 「あんな、チャリってのはな、フツーＡ地点からＢ地点へ移動するためにチョッパるもんだろ」
lines.english: “Listen, you usually steal a bike to get from point A to point B, right?”

lines.japanese: 「したら現実的に考えてみ。Ａ地点で盗まれたチャリがＡ地点で見つかるはずはねえの。柳木原でパクられたチャリは柳木原にはねえの。な、だろ。じゃあおまえ、そんなん、どこを探せばいいって話だよ」
lines.english: “So think realistically. A bike stolen at point A won't turn up at point A. A bike stolen in Yanagihara won't be in Yanagihara. Right? Right. So where the hell am I supposed to look?”

lines.japanese: 「しゃらくせえ……」
lines.english: “Smart-ass...”

lines.japanese: 我ながら明快な説明だったと思う。しかしパル兄貴（本人は知らないパル姐さんのもうひとつの仇名。主にキレモード入ったときに使用）は聞きわけてくれなかった。
lines.english: I thought I’d explained it clearly. But Big Brother Paru—another nickname Paru didn’t know she had, mostly used when she went into rage mode—wouldn’t listen.

lines.japanese: 「四の五のぬかしてんじゃねえや、シャバ僧！　ああッ！？　てめコラ、気合が足んねンだァ！」
lines.english: “Quit fucking arguing, you little amateur! Huh?! You bastard, you’ve got no fucking spirit!”

lines.japanese: 顎の先を上下させてヤンキーフレーバーな爆発。小娘がびくりと肩をすぼませる。俺は怒鳴り声が飛びこんできた方の耳に、小指で詮をした。
lines.english: Her chin pumped as she exploded in full delinquent style. The girl flinched and drew in her shoulders. I plugged the ear she’d shouted into with my little finger.

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、でけー声出すなって……んな、どこ探しゃいいかも分かんねーのに、気合もクソもねえっつの。俺はただの雑用代行屋で、私立探偵とか興信所じゃねーの」
lines.english: “Shut up, don’t yell... What the fuck’s spirit got to do with it when I don’t even know where to look? I’m just a guy who does errands, not a private detective or an investigation agency.”

lines.japanese: 「かァー！　呆れたね、呆れたもんだねこいつぁ、ええッ？　やりもしねえうちから諦める、その負け犬根性があたしゃ気にいらないってんだよコンチキショー！」
lines.english: “Unbelievable! Would you listen to him? Huh? It’s that loser mentality of yours—giving up before you even try—that I can’t stand, goddammit!”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ。あのさ、おばちゃんさ。精神論・根性論も結構だけどさ、実際問題ってのがあるわけじゃん」
lines.english: “Listen, lady. Come on. All that talk about spirit and guts is great, but there are practical limits here.”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってやんでえ、この糞ガキっ！　手足ふんじばってアタマかち割るよ！」
lines.english: “What the fuck are you saying, you little shit? I’ll tie your arms and legs and crack your head open!”

lines.japanese: 兄貴が車体の外側からカウンターに手を突っ込み、クラッシュ前のでっかい氷を振りかざした。おー怖え。仕方なく俺は、後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら小娘に向きなおった。
lines.english: Big Brother reached over the counter from outside the van and brandished a huge chunk of ice waiting to be crushed. Oooh, scary. With no choice, I scratched the back of my head and turned to the girl.

lines.japanese: 「あー……んじゃさ」
lines.english: “Uh... all right, then.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: 怒れるパル兄貴が監視してる。やつに細々とした恩があるのは確かだ。どうしたもんか。俺は尖らせた舌先で頬の裏にできた口内炎を気にしながら、適当な解決策をぼんやりと考えた。
lines.english: Angry Big Brother Paru was watching. It was true I owed her a bunch of little favors. What now? Prodding the sore inside my cheek with the tip of my tongue, I vaguely thought about whatever might solve this.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうだ。分かった。おまえ、モンキ行け」
lines.english: “Ah, I've got it. Go to Monki.”
“Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、あんじゃんモンキホーテ。ほら、駅の向こうッ側。な、そこ行け。マジ、爆安の殿堂だからモンキホーテ」
lines.english: “You know—Monki Hote. Across the station. Go there. Seriously, Monki Hote is the palace of blowout bargains.”

lines.japanese: 俺は新品のチャリが破格値で買える大型ディスカウントショップを教えてやった。
lines.english: I told her about the big discount store where she could buy a new bike at a ridiculous price.
“Ahhh...”

lines.japanese: やつは白い首を見せるように顎を上向けた。
lines.english: She tilted her chin up, showing her pale neck.

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、お気遣いありがとうございます。やー、でも新しい自転車を買うお金がないわけじゃなくて、あの自転車を取りもどしたいんです私」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Thank you for the thought. But it isn't that I can't afford a new bicycle. I want *that* bicycle back.”

lines.japanese: ミニバンの中からごとりと大きな音がした。パルさんが氷の塊を戻した音だ。
lines.english: A heavy clunk came from inside the minivan. Paru putting the block of ice back.

lines.japanese: 「はァ、なるほどなるほど。ねーちゃん、そいつになにか、大切な想い出でもあるわけだね」
lines.english: “Ahh, I see, I see. That bicycle carries some precious memory for you, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、はい、話せば長くなるんですけど……」
lines.english: “Yes, it’s a long story, but...”

lines.japanese: パルさんの優しい声に対する小娘の返答は、中途半端な余韻を残して終わった。
lines.english: The girl’s reply to Paru’s gentle voice ended on an unfinished note.

lines.japanese: やつは一度まぶたを伏せた。しかし場に一瞬の沈黙が訪れると、ほころんだ間を繕うような白々しさでふたたび口を開いた。
lines.english: Her eyelids lowered once. But when a moment of silence opened, she began again with the false brightness of someone hastening to patch the gap.

lines.japanese: 「あー……えーと、そう、あれは暑い夏の日でした」
lines.english: “Ah... let's see. Yes. It was a hot summer day.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、回想シーンいいから」
lines.english: “We can skip the flashback.”

lines.japanese: 俺はすかさずツッコミを入れた。
lines.english: I fired back without missing a beat.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、そんな大事なもんなら、とりあえずお巡りさんにでも相談しとけば」
lines.english: “Listen, if it's that important, why not start by talking to a cop?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、盗難届けはさっき出してきましてー」
lines.english: “Ah, yes, I just filed a theft report...”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh, okay.”

lines.japanese: だったらあとは役人の仕事だ。盗難自転車一台にかまけるほど日本の警察は暇じゃないと思うけど、少なくとも無力な便利屋さんに頼るよりは気休めになるだろう。
lines.english: Then the rest was the authorities’ job. I didn’t think Japan’s police had enough free time to fuss over one stolen bicycle, but at least that would offer more comfort than asking a helpless handyman.

lines.japanese: 「見つかるとイイデスネ。そんじゃ」
lines.english: “I Do Hope You Find It. Well, later.”

lines.japanese: 俺は腰を折って深々と頭を下げる──みたいに、足元のバケツを拾いあげた。
lines.english: I bent at the waist and bowed deeply—or that was how it looked as I picked up the bucket at my feet.

lines.japanese: 「でっ」
lines.english: “Ow.”

lines.japanese: 背筋を伸ばしたとき、後ろから脳天はたき落としが叩きこまれた。
lines.english: When I straightened, a smack crashed down on the crown of my head from behind.

lines.japanese: 「バカヤロ。だから『そんじゃ』じゃないってんだよ」
lines.english: “Idiot. I keep telling you, you don't get to say ‘later.’”

lines.japanese: 「ってえな、ぽんぽんぽんぽん叩くんじゃねえよ。キューティクル剥がれちゃうだろ、てめえ」
lines.english: “Goddammit, quit smacking me over and over. You’ll strip the cuticle right off my hair, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「なに言ってんだい、物臭坊主が。どうせろくなヘアケアもしてないくせによ」
lines.english: “What are you talking about, you lazy brat? As if you take any care of your hair.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんでてめえにそんなこと分かんだよ。分かんねーだろ。ワイルドな外見に似合わず、意外にモイスチャーミルク効果バリバリのシャンプーとか愛用してるかもしんねーだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? How the fuck do you know? You don’t know. Despite my wild looks, maybe I swear by some shampoo with a seriously kick-ass moisturizing-milk effect.”

lines.japanese: 「あはっ」
lines.english: “Aha!”

lines.japanese: 舌戦を交わす俺たちの横で、小娘がちらりと白い歯を覗かせた。なかなか愛嬌のある八重歯が見えた。笑ってんじゃねえよ、と言いかけたがなんとなくやめた。
lines.english: Beside us as we traded fire, the girl briefly showed her white teeth. I glimpsed a rather charming little snaggletooth. I almost told her not to laugh, but for some reason stopped myself.

lines.japanese: パルさんの目ン玉も一瞬そっちへ向いたみたいだった。
lines.english: Paru's eyes seemed to flick her way for an instant too.

lines.japanese: だけどすぐに俺の方へ戻ってきて、観客を意識した芝居臭さでにやりと笑う。
lines.english: But right away they came back to me, and she grinned theatrically, conscious of her audience.

lines.japanese: 「ほぉー、そんなら教えてもらおうじゃねえか。なんだい、なんだいそのモイスチャーミルクってなァ」
lines.english: “Ohhh, then let’s have you teach us. What, what’s this moisturizing milk?”

lines.japanese: 始まった。この、くっちゃべりとお節介が好きな下町生まれのねーちゃんは、舌の回りの悪いガキんちょがいるとたまにこうして会話の門戸を広げようとするんだ。しょーもない、俺はいつものように返すだけだ。
lines.english: Here we go. This downtown-born woman who loved gossip and meddling sometimes opened up the gates of conversation like this for a kid who wasn’t good with words. Ridiculous. I just had to answer like usual.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだよ、モイスチャーミルクも知らねーのかよ。モイスチャーミルクはアレだよ、だから……あの、なんか髪の毛とか、しっとりなめらか潤うんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What, you don’t even know moisturizing milk? Moisturizing milk’s, you know... uh, it makes your hair all, like, moist and smooth and hydrated.”

lines.japanese: 「はああ、大したもんだねえ。で？　そりゃまたどういった原理で？」
lines.english: “Ohhh, that’s quite something. And? By what principle does it do that?”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、原理とかそんな、理屈じゃねーんだよ。とにかくハンパねーんだよ、マジすげえぞモイスチャーミルク。なんか髪の毛とか、しっとりなめらか潤うんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up, it’s not about principles or fucking logic. It’s just incredible. Seriously amazing, moisturizing milk. Makes your hair all, like, moist and smooth and hydrated.”

lines.japanese: 「へッ、なにが理屈じゃねえだィ、話ンなんないね」
lines.english: “Heh, what’s this ‘not about logic’ nonsense? No talking to you.”

lines.japanese: パルさんは高座に上がった落語家みたいに大きく肩をすくめた。ひでえ大根芝居。それから一呼吸して、片方の肩をたったひとりの観客へ突きだした。
lines.english: Paru gave a big shrug like a storyteller onstage. Terrible ham acting. Then, after a breath, she pointed one shoulder at her audience of one.

lines.japanese: 「ねーちゃん、あんたなら知ってるかい、モイスチャーなんとか」
lines.english: “Miss, do you know? Moisturizing-whatever?”

lines.japanese: 客待ちの受付嬢みたいにお行儀よく微笑んでいた小娘が、不意に呼ばれてポケッと口を開けた。
lines.english: The girl had been smiling primly like a receptionist awaiting customers. Called on without warning, she opened her mouth blankly.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい……モイスチャーミルク、えっと……」
lines.english: “Ah, yes... Moisturizing milk, um...”

lines.japanese: ちら、ちら、と高速の視線が俺＆パルさんの表情をかすめていった。
lines.english: Her gaze flicked rapidly across my face and Paru's.

lines.japanese: 「なんか、髪の毛とか、しっとりなめらか潤うらしいです」
lines.english: “Apparently it makes your hair all, like, moist and smooth and hydrated.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが満足げに鼻を鳴らした。ぐずぐずと「さあ」だの「分かりません」だのと言うようだったら、ただの話嫌いか人間嫌い。そういうやつには姐さんも深入りしない。
lines.english: Paru snorted, satisfied. If she’d stalled with “Who knows” or “I don’t know,” she’d just have been somebody who hated talking or hated people. Paru didn’t press those people too far.

lines.japanese: でもこいつはパルさんの眼鏡にかなった。仕方ない、祝儀にツッコミを入れてやろう。
lines.english: But this one met Paru’s approval. Fine, I’d give her a comeback as a congratulatory gift.

lines.japanese: 「てめソレ、俺のコメントまんまじゃねーか。パクってんじゃねえよ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, that's my comment word for word. Don't steal my material. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ははー」
lines.english: “Hahaaa.”

lines.japanese: さっきと同じ愛想のない低音を叩きつけても、やつはもうほとんど怯んだりせず、右手を頭の後ろに添えて眩しそうに目を細めるだけだった。
lines.english: Even with the same unfriendly bass voice hurled at her as before, she hardly shrank back now. Just put her right hand behind her head and narrowed her eyes as if the light was bright.

lines.japanese: 「えー、どういう原理なんでしょうねー、モイスチャーミルク効果。なんでしっとり滑らか潤っちゃうんですかねー」
lines.english: “Ehhh, I wonder what the principle is, the moisturizing-milk effect. Why does it make things all moist and smooth and hydrated...?”

lines.japanese: 少女らしいにこやかな、しかしこっそり会話の温度を調べるような、どこか含みのある調子。
lines.english: The tone was sunny and girlish, yet carried something beneath it, as though she were secretly taking the conversation's temperature.

lines.japanese: こいつ……自分からパルさんの誘いに乗ってきたよ。ふん、ガキのくせになかなか読むじゃねえか。
lines.english: This kid... She'd taken Paru up on the invitation and jumped into the exchange on her own. Hmph. Not bad at reading the room for a brat.

lines.japanese: 「あー、あれですかねー、ジンクピリチオンとか関係してるんですかねー」
lines.english: “Ahh, maybe it’s, you know, got something to do with zinc pyrithione...?”

lines.japanese: つーか打ちかえしてきたよ。洒落たマネしてくれる。そっちがそう来るなら、こっちは──
lines.english: Hell, she had returned my shot. Stylish move. If that was how she meant to play it, then I would—
